decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed slowed the pace of its rate cuts, lowering the benchmark rate by 25 basis points instead of the larger 50-basis-point cuts seen previously.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The secondary rate charged on direct bank loans was also reduced by 25 basis points, matching the move in the main policy rate.

changes.quote: Economic activity remains soft, with underlying inflation likely to edge lower from relatively modest levels.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted ongoing economic softness while anticipating that inflation will drift slightly lower.

changes.quote: To be sure, weakness in demand shows signs of abating, but those signs are preliminary and tentative.
changes.explanation: While there are early signs that economic weakness might be leveling off, the Fed considers these indicators very uncertain.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to believe that, against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.
changes.explanation: The Fed maintained its official stance that future economic risks remain tilted toward ongoing weakness rather than inflation.

tone_quotes.quote: Economic activity remains soft, with underlying inflation likely to edge lower from relatively modest levels.

The Committee continues to believe that, against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 14.59% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.13% and moved -4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.02% would fall by about $8.06 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 5.5%, and employers added an average of -292k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (November 2001); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -7 bp on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will continue to monitor whether early signs of stabilization in demand turn into a sustained recovery. Upcoming meetings will likely depend on incoming economic data regarding output and labor market conditions.
